scope: Inventory and containment of the server-side PropertyRecord graph's global dependencies. No MCP tools, HTTP endpoints, auth infrastructure, schema, Pilot data, Production, payment/Ripple, UI or CAM repair.

headline.outcome: No unsafe undeclared dependency was found, and that is now a measurement rather than an absence of evidence.
headline.detail: The graph reaches for 29 names. All 29 are classified. The 19 browser-only ones live in the render and action halves of tenant-space.js and property-workspace.js; the widest property this graph can be handed — two tenants, two disputes, eleven timeline events covering every attachment kind, a CAM reconciliation with results, lease document URLs, three invoices — reaches none of them.
headline.why_that_needed_proving: M2 measured only what five thin scenarios happened to touch. A window.showToast on a branch no fixture reached would have been live, undeclared, and invisible to it.

what_M3_added: tools/global-dependency-inventory.js — the static half of the measurement, including BARE identifiers, which no window.* scan can see
a "rich" scenario in the runtime harness that exercises disputes, every attachment kind, CAM results and lease documents
module-instance identity checks with negative controls, so two copies of the same logic cannot assemble one record unnoticed
environment variables treated as runtime dependencies and inventoried alongside browser globals

appendPropertyTimelineEvent.why: a WRITE path — it appends an event to the property record, and must never be reachable from a read-only server module

AuthService.why: browser SESSION state — the current signed-in user

currentProperty.why: browser SESSION state — the property open in the tab

DocViewer.why: opens a document in a DOM overlay; tenant-space.js reaches for it only from click handlers, never from assemble()

esc.why: HTML escaper; each file has its own local fallback

FileReader.why: bare browser global at tenant-space.js:1114, inside an upload handler assemble() never reaches

generateTenantStatement.why: renders a tenant statement into the page; a UI action reached only from a click handler

isStoredDocumentRef.why: storage-reference helper; falls back to a local test

openDisputeWorkspace.why: navigates the browser to the dispute panel; reached only from a click handler in tenant-space.js

saveProperty.why: a WRITE path; must never be reachable from a read-only server module

savePropertyNow.why: a WRITE path; must never be reachable from a read-only server module

Selectors.why: pure logic, but calls a BARE ReviewEngine identifier that only a second global could satisfy. Reads {} here; the hydrator reports the degradation as attention.without_selectors_readiness.

showToast.why: transient UI notification; every call site guards it with if (window.showToast), so absence is the handled branch

switchWorkspaceTab.why: moves the browser tab focus between workspace panels; navigation, with no meaning on a server

VERCEL_ENV.why: selects production vs pilot; absent ⇒ pilot, which is the fail-safe direction

XRPL_NETWORK.why: read by _pilot-target.js for other callers; unused by the hydrator

MoneyCents.why: cam-pool.js and variance-breakdown.js fall back to require('./money-cents.js')

SourceValues.why: cam-pool.js and money-cents.js fall back to require('./source-values.js')

PropertyReference.why: pure; supplied by the allow-list, and read at call time by property-workspace.js:86 with no fallback

selectors_decision.selectors_js_is_pure: zero document, zero localStorage, zero fetch, zero timers, zero innerHTML
selectors_decision.review_engine_is_pure_too: its six "document" occurrences are the English word inside strings and comments, not the DOM API
selectors_decision.first_blocker: selectors.js calls a BARE ReviewEngine identifier at 7 call sites, never window.ReviewEngine. A sealed shim cannot satisfy a bare identifier; only global.ReviewEngine could, which is exactly the second global workaround the phase forbids.
selectors_decision.second_blocker: review-engine.js:142 resolves SourceValues as (window.SourceValues) || null with NO require fallback, and its own error message states the cost: "every lease will read as missing its area". Supplying ReviewEngine without also supplying SourceValues would silently corrupt every readiness answer.
selectors_decision.cost_of_inclusion: editing selectors.js (a browser-loaded file), broadening the allow-list by three names, and changing PropertyRecord semantics by adding attention items
selectors_decision.what_exclusion_costs: attention is composed from fewer inputs; the hydrator reports it as degraded["attention.without_selectors_readiness"], and meta.unavailable is untouched because attention IS composed

runtime_measurement.each_of_which: is classified module (require fallback verified in source) or browser_only (Selectors, reported as degradation)

removed_or_contained.removed: nothing — no unsafe undeclared dependency existed to remove after M1b and M2
contained: the three dual-resolution module names resolve through require() on the server, and the resolved instance is asserted identical to the declared dependency set
the 19 browser-only names are unreachable from assemble(), measured under the widest fixture, and any future reachability shows up as a new undeclared read that fails the suite
the six environment reads live in one file, and the unset direction resolves to pilot, never production
removed_or_contained.dead_code_removed: the probe's identityExpected field, which a mutation exposed as output nothing read once the expected polarity moved into the test

gaps_the_first_run_exposed: S-unclassified-hidden and S-classify-always-module — nothing fed an UNKNOWN global through inventory(); now a fixture repo does (A7a/A7b)
F-disputes-not-passed and F-timeline-not-passed — the rich fixture could be gutted and D5 would still pass; the record content is now asserted (D9a-D9f)
F-sameinstance-blind — per-name literals could be hardcoded true; the check is now table-driven with negative controls (F1a-F6)

C-shimmed-list-widened — my first version of this mutant was MALFORMED (a duplicate object key that the later entry overwrote, so it was a no-op). Rewritten to reclassify an existing entry, and it dies.

mutation_m1b.survivor: D-prune-removed — the same equivalent mutant reported and explained in M1b, unchanged

failing_assertions: 4 control(s) promise an object and navigate generically
review actions do not carry the tenant id
full_regression.baseline_check: the identical two assertions fail at c3dbee9, before M1b — preserved as the known unrelated baseline, not fixed or repinned
